about: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery was founded on Keuka Lake in 1962 by a Ukrainian-born viticulturist who insisted, against the conventional wisdom of the day, that European vinifera grapes could survive Finger Lakes winters. Four generations on, the family has kept pushing into new varieties. In 2006 Frank’s grandson Fred bought land on the east side of Seneca Lake in Hector and began planting Grüner Veltliner, Austria’s signature white grape, building what is now one of the largest plantings of it in the United States.

This wine comes entirely from that Seneca Estate, vines planted in 2007 in deep Honeoye silt loam within the lake’s so-called “Banana Belt,” the warmest mesoclimate in the Finger Lakes. In 2023 a once-in-a-century freeze in mid-May cost the vineyard between 10 and 50 percent of its buds, and the smaller crop that survived ripened with real concentration. The grapes were destemmed, pressed directly, and fermented cool in stainless steel without malolactic fermentation, keeping the wine taut and unoaked.

The winery’s notes point to cool scents of guava, rosewater and candied lime, with apricot and papaya on the finish, and a sleek, vivid palate built on focus and precision. Critics agreed: Wine Enthusiast gave it 92 points and named it No. 5 on its Top 100 Best Buys of 2025, a global list of wines at $20 and under.
